$comment: The naming rules every public API follows, with the deliberate exceptions. Read by scripts/component-manifest.mjs into packages/react/manifest.json.

rules.names: Components and their parts are PascalCase; hooks start with use; acronyms stay in capitals (AIIcon, MCPServerCard).
rules.values: A controlled value is value with onValueChange; open state is open with onOpenChange, and defaultOpen when uncontrolled.
rules.state: state is a lifecycle: streaming, running, complete, failed. status is whether host data is there: ready, loading, denied, unavailable, error, stale.
rules.labels: States render as words ("Connected", "Needs review"), never as the raw value.
rules.progress: loading is data on its way; pending is a request waiting for the host; busy is an action of this component in progress.
rules.styling: Style through --ai-* variables, className on the root and data-part hooks; generated class names are not an API.
rules.hosts: A clicked button is a request: components show the host's answer, never an assumed outcome.

exceptions.reason: One prop carries both streaming and availability, so it is named for the lifecycle.
It reports an edit request for the host to apply, not a new value.
A form holds several values at once.
